I farm with my age, my hands, and my water in mind. I am 68, there are only 2 people in my household, and I have worked this land for 50 years, so I will not spread myself too thin on the most labor-hungry crops. I will keep a bigger share in maize because it is steady and easier for me to manage, and I will still plant some cotton and chili for cash, but not too much because they need more spraying, picking, and close watching. I will keep cabbage and Chinese cabbage in the plan because they fit my usual way of farming and give me quicker returns, and with my well irrigation I can support them when the weather turns dry. I will use mostly hybrid or improved seed where it helps stand establishment and yield, but I will not push fertilizer to extremes because I want dependable production, not waste. I will use ploughing on the broader field crops and rotary tillage on the vegetable land because that is how I can prepare the beds well enough without making the work heavier than it needs to be. My plan is to balance cash income, household labor, irrigation capacity, and risk across the whole 15.5 mu.
